chunks: He said: He (my father) used to attend the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) for the service he had been assigned to.

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa would come at the time of dawn every night to learn news of the illness of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). There was a messenger who used to go between Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and my father; whenever he arrived, Ahmad would rise and my father would be alone with him.

So one night I went out and Ahmad rose from the gathering and my father was alone with the messenger, and Ahmad circled around and stood where he could hear the speech. The messenger said to my father: 'Your Master conveys his greetings upon you and says to you: I am going to pass away, and the authority (Imamate) will pass to my son Ali, and his right upon you after me is what was my right upon you after my father.'

Then the messenger departed and Ahmad returned to his place and said to my father: 'What did he say to you?' He said: 'Good.' He said: 'I heard what he said, so why do you conceal it?' and he repeated what he had heard. So my father said to him: 'God has forbidden upon you what you did, because God the Exalted says:
So preserve this testimony, for perhaps we will need it one day, and beware of revealing it before its proper time.'

When morning came, my father wrote out the message in ten scrolls and sealed them, and handed them over to ten notables of the community, saying: 'If death should befall me before I request them back from you, then open them and act upon what is in them.'

When Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away, my father mentioned that he did not leave his house until about four hundred persons had pledged allegiance upon his hands, and the leaders of the community gathered at Muhammad ibn al-Faraj's home to discuss this matter. So Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to my father informing him of their gathering with him and that if not for fear of publicity he would have come with them, and he asked him to come.

So my father mounted and went to him and found the people assembled with him. They said to my father: 'What do you say regarding this matter?' My father said to those who had the scrolls: 'Produce the scrolls.' They produced them, and he said to them: 'This is what I was commanded with.' Some of them said: 'We would have liked there to be another witness with you in this matter.'

He said to them: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has already brought him to you. This is Abu Ja'far al-Ash'ari; he will testify for me that he heard this message,' and he asked him to testify with what he had. But Ahmad denied that he had heard anything of this. So my father challenged him to the mubahala (mutual imprecation).

When it was pressed against him, he said: 'I did hear that, but this was an honor I wished would be for a man from the Arabs, not for a man from the non-Arabs.' And the people did not depart until they all affirmed the truth.

key_terms.الأمر: The authority/command — referring to the Imamate
key_terms.الرِّقَاع: Scrolls/parchments — used to preserve the testimony
key_terms.المبَاهَلَة: Mubahala — invocation of divine curse upon the liar in a dispute
key_terms.الْعِصَابَة: The community/group — referring to the Shia community
key_terms.صَائِرٌ: Passing to/being transferred to — the succession of authority
key_terms.مَاضٍ: Going to pass away — the Imam's declaration of his imminent death

ai.seo_question: How was Imam Ali al-Hadi designated as the tenth Imam after Imam al-Jawad?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by the son of al-Khayrani (a doorman serving Imam al-Jawad), describes the secret proclamation of Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS) as the tenth Imam following the death of his father Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS). The narration reveals how Imam al-Jawad's deathbed message designating his son 'Ali as his successor was covertly transmitted through a messenger, witnessed by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa (who initially tried to conceal it due to ethnic prejudice against non-Arabs), and ultimately confirmed before hundreds of the Shia community's leaders. The story illustrates how the imamate designation was carefully documented and preserved through sealed scrolls to guard against suppression, and how the community's acceptance of the next Imam was achieved through dramatic confrontation and the threat of mubahala (mutual cursing).
